svg.title: The grader ladder
svg.desc: A ladder of four grader types, from bottom to top. Code checks, such as schema validity, field equality, membership, and date rules: instant, free, and deterministic, but only for what a program can decide. Reference comparison, such as exact or normalized match, key facts, or similarity to a labeled answer: fast and cheap, but brittle when many outputs are correct. LLM judge, such as rubric criteria or pairwise preferences: handles meaning at scale, but is slower, costs money, and has biases, so it must be calibrated. Human review, by domain experts giving pass or fail with a critique: the ground truth, but slow and expensive, so it is used for calibration labels and hard cases. An arrow on the left shows cost, latency, and variance rising from bottom to top; an arrow on the right shows nuance rising. Push every check as low on the ladder as it can go.

g.text: domain experts give pass or fail with a written critique

schema validity, field equality, membership, date rules, length

Push every check as low on the ladder as it can go.
